statement: Historical arithmetic audit of the 4 September Paper B snapshot; passing checks do not establish the analytic estimates withdrawn in the 9 September conditional revision. Paper B companion audit ledger docs/theory/paper_b_audit_ledger.md and research.juggler_sequence.paper_b_audit. Machine layer: the exact identities of Lemma 4.3 (one-signed remainder 0 ≤ E ≤ (3/8)(X−1)^{−1/2}, gap identity), Lemma 5.1(i)–(iv) (0 ≤ R ≤ (3/16) v^{−1/2}; double-gap identity; carry as sawtooth difference; ΔΔY = F_κ(m), |j| ≤ 3, the offset/second-difference split with its numerical ranges and the |G′| bound; the master identity with all four brackets ≤ 2) and Lemma 6.2 hold on 360 random odd starts across 10⁴ ≤ n ≤ 2·10¹⁴ at 60–120 digits; the standing estimates (E1)–(E6) contain the observed values at P = 10⁶, 10⁸, 10¹⁰; the cell inventory 1.5 h P^{1/2} + 1 with lengths [2/3, 0.95] P^{1/2}/h holds exhaustively at P = 10⁵; 98 displayed P-power comparisons of the kernel argument hold as exact rational statements. Companion file docs/theory/paper_b_audit_ledger.md. The printed Step 5b |B|<1 is withdrawn: frozen B has constant size at most 6. Three corrections, none changing a statement: Lemma 4.3’s proof printed f″ = (3/8)(X−t)^{−1/2} (correct (3/4)); Lemma 3.9’s printed ℓ^∞ operator norm 288 is the ℓ¹ norm (the ℓ^∞ norm is 232; c₇ = 1/288 remains valid); Lemma 6.2 now displays the two Lagrange remainders (orders n^{−45/16}, n^{−81/16}) instead of absorbing them into coefficients without slack. Observation only: |K_c(P)| at P ≤ 3·10⁵ is 0.4–1.2 times (P/2)^{1/2}, square-root scale. A script check is consistency of what is printed, not a proof, and not an independent human verification Fourth correction (4 September 2026): Step 5b interpolant is the frozen-shape Lemma 5.2b, local leading -135/1024, b = -405/176, lambda_0 in [0.35, 2.6]; the moving-gap (c F_sm) = 243/128 is a different object and is withdrawn. Theorem 5.3 unchanged. Fifth correction (4 September 2026): Theorem 6.1 Step E is the same frozen-versus-smooth error one theorem later; offset leftover 81/512, window-centre 324/512, composite 243/512, B = 27/32 k j nu^{3/8}; zero-offset lambda_0' = 1095/1024 k h1 h2 nu^{-5/8}; the withdrawn 405/512 and 8.27 differentiated the moving total phase (k/2) nu^{27/8}. The 1-1/96 exponent is unchanged. Sixth correction (4 September 2026): Theorem 5.3 is the monomial c = (3k/4) n^{9/8}; Step 5b zero-offset |B| is (9/32) k beta1 beta2 n^{-9/8} with |B| <= 6; rho_0 ratios of Lemma 5.2b are O(P^{-1/4}).

Publication review 9 September 2026: the analytic claim below is not established by Paper B and is retained only as a historical research target. The revised paper gives conditional implications, not this analytic proof. See docs/theory/paper_b_review.md. Historical target: Paper B §3.5, Lemma 4.10 and Theorems 4.11–4.12 (nested and triple parity discrepancy on sub-dyadic intervals, with a slow twist). For every ε > 0 there is P₀ such that for P ≥ P₀, every interval I ⊆ (P, 2P] of length Y ≥ P^{1/2}, every (a,b,c) ∈ {0,1}³ ∖ {0} and every slow twist g(n) = (ℓ/2) n^{9/16} with |ℓ| ≤ P^{1/24}: |Σ_{n ∈ I odd} ψ(n^{3/2})^a ψ(m^{3/2})^b ψ(v^{1/2})^c e(g(n))| ≤ Y P^{−1/24+ε} (Theorem 4.12; Theorem 4.11 is the case c = 0). Proof: Steps 1–7 of Theorems 4.4/4.7 run over I with the number of summands Y in place of P; every cost is proportional to Y except three absolute terms — the two partial end cells 5.2 (jh)^{−1/2} P^{3/8}, the pure passenger 3.8 P^{7/16}, the majorant end cells 17 P^{1/4} — which fall below Y P^{−1/24} for Y ≥ P^{1/2}; the twist survives the Weyl differencing as e(Δ_{2h} g) with total variation ≤ 0.26 P^{−5/16} over the block and is removed by one partial summation (Lemma 4.10) against the untwisted differenced sums on initial sub-intervals, whose bound is nondecreasing in the length; in the single-smooth-sum cases the twist’s curvature 0.13 P^{1/24−23/16} is dominated by powers of P. Corollary 4.13 (the OOEEE production on even blocks): for m′ ≥ 2 and I(m′) = [m′^{32/9}, (m′+1)^{32/9}), #{odd n ∈ I(m′) : word₅(n) = OOEEE, J⁵(n) = m′} = (1/16)#{odd n ∈ I(m′)} + O(|I(m′)| m′^{−4/27+ε}), via the nesting bound 0 ≤ n^{9/16} − v^{1/4} ≤ n^{−15/16}, an Erdős–Turán/Kusmin–Landau bound Y P^{−1/16} for the exceptional set, and a Vaaler expansion of the fifth letter whose modes are the slow twists. This discharges Hypothesis L of Paper C (Appendix C) to a Paper B theorem; Paper B remains a working draft. Not a halt theorem.
